claim: Shona verb phonotactics impose nonlocal vowel-height harmony: /a/ is freely distributed, while mid vowels and following high vowels have restricted distributions controlled by preceding vowel height.
normalized_environment: V1 ... V2 on vowel projection; height co-occurrence restrictions
scope: verbs; Hayes & Wilson summarize Fortune 1955, Beckman 1997, Riggle 1999
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Harmony is closest to exceptionless in verbs but not completely exceptionless; idiophones and borrowings supply violations.

claim: Mid /e, o/ are restricted noninitially: noninitial /e/ requires a preceding /e/ trigger, and noninitial /o/ requires a preceding /o/ trigger in the descriptive generalization used by Hayes & Wilson.
normalized_environment: e noninitial ⇒ preceding e; o noninitial ⇒ preceding o
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Small corpus counts violate the categorical descriptive generalization, including 3 a...e, 4 u...e, and 1 u...o tokens; the corpus includes idiophones and borrowings.

claim: High /i/ is disfavored after /e/ or /o/, and /u/ is disfavored after /o/; suffixes alternate in height to satisfy these restrictions.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The /o/ trigger is gradient/weak: o...i and o...u are underrepresented rather than absent.

claim: The /o/ harmony trigger is demonstrably weaker than /e/: o...i and o...u occur 23 and 20 times respectively and are underrepresented, whereas e...i occurs only twice.
scope: 4,399 Shona verbs from Hannan 1959 online dictionary
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Hayes & Wilson state this weak-trigger property had not, to their knowledge, been previously noticed.

claim: Every Wargamay word begins with a consonant; vowel sequences are prohibited; consonant clusters are prohibited word-initially and word-finally.
scope: Dixon 1981 phonotactics as summarized by Hayes & Wilson
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Hayes & Wilson removed a handful of blatant violations from training, including loanwords with an initial cluster or final cluster.

claim: All consonants except the anterior approximants /r, l/ may occur word-initially.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The loanword [lajn] 'line' is an explicit blatant violation removed from the learner's training set.

claim: Only a subset of sonorants /m, n, ɲ, l, r, j/ may occur word-finally; final obstruents and other consonant classes are excluded.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: A loanword with a final obstruent is among the blatant violations removed from training.

claim: Among licit final consonants, /m/ and /r/ are very rare: four vocabulary items end in /m/ and eleven in /r/, each contributing under about 1% of consonant-final inflected learning forms; other permitted final consonants reach at least 5%.
scope: Dixon vocabulary plus Hayes & Wilson inflected training corpus
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The learner overpenalizes these rare but grammatical finals, illustrating why corpus underrepresentation must not be converted into a categorical ban.

claim: Hayes & Wilson explicitly exclude several forms that blatantly violate native Wargamay phonotactics, including three loanwords: [drajga] 'tracker' with an initial cluster, [gaːgu... ] 'cockroach' with a final obstruent, and [lajn] 'line' with initial /l/ and a final cluster.
normalized_environment: loanwords may violate native edge constraints
exceptions_or_counterexamples: These forms are exceptions by design and should not be used to weaken the native-stratum restriction without a lexical-stratum distinction.
